function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
The debate over who is the greatest basketball player ever has raged for decades, and while opinions vary, most analysts, former players, and fans point to **Michael Jordan** as the definitive choice.

### Why Michael Jordan?

| Category | Jordan’s Record |
|----------|-----------------|
| **Championships** | 6 NBA titles (1991‑1993, 1996‑1998) |
| **MVP Awards** | 5 regular‑season MVPs (1988‑1991, 1996) |
| **Scoring Titles** | 10 scoring titles (1979‑80, 1987‑88, 1988‑89, 1989‑90, 1990‑91, 1991‑92, 1992‑93, 1993‑94, 1994‑95, 1995‑96) |
| **All‑Star Appearances** | 14 consecutive All‑Stars (1985‑1998) |
| **Defensive Impact** | 9 All‑Defensive First Team selections |
| **Clutch Performance** | 30+ points in 12 Finals games; 3 game‑winning shots in 1998 Finals |
| **Cultural Influence** | Global icon; helped popularize the NBA worldwide; iconic “Air” brand |

### How He Stands Out

1. **Consistency & Longevity** – Averaging 30.12 points per game over his career, Jordan maintained elite performance across two separate eras (pre‑and post‑1995).  
2. **Versatility** – While known for scoring, he was also a solid defender, rebounder, and playmaker (averaging 5.3 assists per game).  
3. **Mental Game** – His competitive drive (“I can’t accept failure”) set a standard for professionalism and work ethic.  
4. **Impact on the Game** – Jordan’s style—high-flying dunks, acrobatic finishes, and fearless drives—redefined how the sport is played and marketed.

### Counterpoints & Other Candidates

| Player | Strengths | Weaknesses |
|--------|-----------|------------|
| **LeBron James** | Versatile all‑rounder; longevity; 4 championships; 4 MVPs | No perfect Finals record; early career injuries |
| **Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar** | 6 championships; 19 seasons; 38,387 points | Not as flashy; defensive accolades fewer |
| **Bill Russell** | 11 championships in 13 seasons | Scoring less relevant; era differences |
| **Magic Johnson** | 5 championships; 3 MVPs; 12 All‑Stars | Career shortened by injury |

While each candidate brings unique strengths, Jordan’s combination of statistical dominance, clutch performances, cultural impact, and championship success places him at the top of most lists.

---

**Bottom line:** In the eyes of historians, analysts, and the majority of fans, Michael Jordan remains the greatest basketball player ever.
